function: GNN learns downlink analog and digital hybrid precoders end-to-end from uplink sounding reference signals, without explicit channel estimation or prediction, maximising sum-rate (pp. 1, 3-5).
system: TDD mmWave BS, Nt=64 antennas, NRF=6 RF chains, K=3 single-antenna mobile users at 30 km/h; narrowband and OFDM wideband; fc=30 GHz; no RIS (pp. 3, 9).
method: Unsupervised GNNs, one per downlink subframe trained in parallel (P-PONet), on a permutation-equivariant BS-user graph; loss is negative sum-rate; Adam optimizer (pp. 5-7, 9).
data_channel: Simulated time-varying geometric mmWave channel (Np=3 paths by default, Doppler, 30 km/h), said to simplify the 3GPP model; 500,000 train, 10,000 validation, 10,000 test samples (pp. 9, 12).
test_conditions: Trained on one configuration, tested on other numbers of paths (2-5), SNRs (-5 to 20 dB), users (2-6) and subcarriers (2-128); also mixed K=3,5 training (pp. 11-12).
baselines: Non-learned: PCSI+WMMSE, PCSI+AO, PCSI+PE, OMP+AO (aging); learned or mixed: PCSI+GNN, E2E+PO (C), OMP+DLCP+AO/GNN/PE (learned predictor [42]), SWOMP+CNN-predictor variants (pp. 10-11).
metrics: Sum-rate versus SRS length, velocity, prediction horizon, SNR, paths, users and subcarriers; required SRS length; FLOPs; inference time; storage (pp. 10-14).
complexity: FLOPs O(NK^2 d^2), about 2.8e7 versus 3.8e7 (OMP+DLCP+AO) and 3.0e7 (OMP+DLCP+PE); CPU inference 29.2 ms versus 49.7 ms; storage 155.6 MB (pp. 13-14).
openness: none: no code or data link; samples generated with the authors' own simulator (p. 9).
q1_support: p. 9: channel "as described in [41]" with footnote 3 "a simplified version of the channel model recommended by 3GPP in [38], adapted for an unpolarized uniform linear array (ULA)"; custom geometric model of Eq. (19), not TR 38.901 itself, no measured data.
q2_support: p. 11: "we evaluate the performance of the well-trained P-PONet and P-PONet-W with the samples generated by a different system configuration from the training setup"; p. 12: "P-PONet-W, trained with M = 4 subcarriers, performs well when tested across a range from 2 to 128 subcarriers".
q3_support: p. 10: PCSI+AO "optimizes the hybrid precoder by an alternating optimization (AO) algorithm proposed in [4]" (non-learned); "methods with explicit channel estimation and prediction, such as OMP+DLCP+AO, OMP+DLCP+GNN and OMP+DLCP+PE" use "using the learning-based method proposed in [42]"; compared on sum-rate (Fig. 6).
q4_support: p. 13: "the orders of FLOPs are around" 2.8e7 for E2E+PO, 3.8e7 and 3.0e7 for OMP+DLCP+AO and OMP+DLCP+PE; "require only 58.8% and 36.0% of the inference time needed by"; Table 9 (p. 14) running times.
q5_support: p. 9: "a total of 520,000 samples are generated based on the narrowband and wideband channel models" with the authors' own simulator; no link to code or data and no availability statement appears anywhere in the paper.
notes: Area 3 although the method also bypasses channel estimation and prediction: the main metric is sum-rate (pp. 9-10). q1 is borderline: footnote 3 calls the channel a simplified version of 3GPP TR 38.901, but the model is the textbook geometric channel of [41] with uniform AoDs and uniform delays, so it was counted as a custom simulator; reviewer to confirm. q3 is borderline: the learned comparators are the authors' own variants (PCSI+GNN, E2E+PO (C) inspired by [26]) and cascades that use the learned predictor of [42] (or a CNN as in [17]); no earlier end-to-end learned hybrid precoder is compared; marked 1 on the paper's wording 'other learning-based methods', reviewer to confirm.
